2.title: The Joint Economic Committee, Republicans
2.description:
Official YouTube site of the Joint Economic Committee Republicans. 
The Joint Economic Committee (JEC) was created when Congress passed the Employment Act of 1946. The primary task is to review economic conditions and to recommend improvements in economic policy.
Chairmanship of the Committee alternates between the Senate and House every Congress. The current chair for the 116th Congress is Senator Mike Lee (R-UT). Members include Senators Tom Cotton (R-AR), Ben Sasse (R-NE), Rob Portman (R-OH), Bill Cassidy (R-LA), Ted Cruz (R-TX), and Representatives David Schweikert (R-AZ 6th District), Darin LaHood (R-IL 18th District), Jaime Herrera Beutler (R-WA 3rd District), and Kenny Marchant (R-TX 24th District). 
Follow us on Twitter or Facebook: @JECRepublicans. Or subscribe to our channel for speeches, insights, and hearing proceedings.

7.title: Chairman Schweikert's Panel 2 Remarks | JEC Hearing on "The Rising Global Scam Economy"
7.description:
On Wednesday, March 25, the U.S. Congress Joint Economic Committee held a hearing, led by Committee Chairman David Schweikert (R-AZ) and Ranking Member Maggie Hassan (D-NH), focused on the threat posed by overseas scam compounds, coordination among federal agencies to fight scams, and the economic impacts of scams on Americans.
This second panel featured leading scams experts from the Government Accountability Office, the Aspen Institute, AARP, and the private sector.
The hearing builds on Chairman Schweikert and Ranking Member Hassan’s efforts to combat scams. Previously, they issued requests to federal agencies about their efforts to crack down on overseas scam networks and issued a scam alert to Americans ahead of the holidays.

Panel II
The Honorable Stewart Baker, Principal, Stewart Baker Consulting PLLC, former Assistant Secretary of DHS for Policy.
Mr. Seto J. Bagdoyan, Director, Forensic Audits & Investigative Service, U.S. Government Accountability Office.
Ms. Kate Griffin, Director of Inclusive Financial System, Aspen Institute Financial Security Program, Aspen Institute.
Ms. Kathy Stokes, Director, Fraud Prevention Programs, AARP.

17.title: Roundtable: Bending the Health Care Cost Curve Through Innovation
17.description:
On Saturday, February 28, Joint Economic Committee Chairman David Schweikert held a healthcare innovation roundtable in Scottsdale, Arizona, bringing together leaders from emerging health and technology companies to discuss how innovation can improve patient access, reduce costs, and modernize care delivery.

The Joint Economic Committee (JEC) roundtable focused on the real-world economics of healthcare innovation. Participants shared insights into how new technologies—ranging from AI-enabled clinical tools to medical devices and performance analytics—are reshaping patient care and system affordability. The discussion also examined policy and regulatory barriers that may be slowing progress.

“The purpose of this discussion [was] to give the Committee a direct understanding of how emerging healthcare and technology companies are changing the economics of care on the ground,” said Chairman Schweikert. “We want to better understand what is working, where innovation is reducing costs and improving outcomes, and what federal policies may need modernization.”

Participants included:
Amy Perry, President and CEO, Banner Health
Jonathan Jeffrey, Chief of Staff, WHOOP
Dr. Adam Oskowitz, Cofounder, Doctronic.AI
Terrence O’Neil, Director of Operations, Calviri
Tom Eisiminger, President and CEO, Regenesis

56.description:
On Wednesday, May 17, Senator Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Chairman of the U.S. Congress Joint Economic Committee (JEC), will hold a hearing titled “Counting the Costs: How a U.S. Default Crisis Harms American Families and Businesses to explore the economic costs of breaching the debt limit and the drastic cuts to important federal programs. 

The United States reached its $31.4 trillion debt limit in January, and the Treasury has been utilizing extraordinary measures since then to ensure that the federal government can continue to pay its bills. Those measures will soon run out, and the federal government may not be able to meet its existing obligations as soon as June 1, unless Congress raises the debt limit. Failing to do so would cause widespread economic harm – costing millions of Americans their jobs, saddling households with higher borrowing costs, jeopardizing payments to millions of seniors and veterans, depressing economic growth, and threatening the country’s credit rating.

11.title: An Invisible Tsunami: ‘Aging Alone’ and Its Effect on Older Americans, Families, and Taxpayers
11.description: Social capital may be most valuable when an individual’s needs are greatest. Old age is a time of life when people often need to rely on family, friends, and other social relationships for care they are no longer able to provide for themselves. If an elderly adult lacks those relationships, however, they may have to lean more heavily on paid professional care, potentially leading to a lower quality of life and higher costs for families and government.

20.title: Reforming the Charitable Deduction
20.description: Rebuilding civil society will require capitalizing on the strengths of America’s associational life to address its weaknesses. One way of doing so is to reform policy so that less of the charitable giving of Americans is subject to taxation. Doing so would be more consistent with the principle that people should not be taxed on money they give away. Reforming the charitable deduction captures the spirit of the Social Capital Project’s approach to policymaking.

21.title: Zoned Out: How School and Residential Zoning Limit Educational Opportunity
21.description: Since housing is the traditional gateway to public education, this paper suggests policymakers consider improving access to educational opportunity by minimizing residential zoning while expanding public school choice policies. Reforming residential zoning supports public school choice efforts by permitting a variety of housing throughout school zones, reducing prices, and improving affordability at every school quality level.

263.description: Rep. Kevin Brady speaks during "Overhauling the Federal Reserve System" hearing. Mr. Brady believes that the Fed is trying to do too much to fix the economy and is only further creating uncertainty. To improve the economy Congress needs to focus on finding the correct fiscal policy.

264.title: Mr. Brady speaks on the idea of a Sound Dollar during Subcommittee hearing
264.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee Kevin Brady, talks about how he defines a sound dollar. He wants a rules based inflation targeting. Preserving the purchasing power of the dollar over time creates the best oppurtunity for strongest growth.

265.title: Rep. Kevin Brady (R-TX) presents testimony during Domestic Monetary Subcommittee hearing
265.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady, presents his testimony during the House Financial Services Subcommittee on Domestic Monetary Policy and Technology hearing "Overhauling the Federal Reserve System". Rep. Brady, recently introduced legislation "Sound Dollar Act" which will reform the Federal Reserve giving it a single mandate of price stability.

266.title: Big Government or Free Markets a comparison between Reagan and Obama recoveries
266.description: Joint Economic Committee Republican staff compares the Obama and Reagan recoveries in the employment sector. The facts clearly show that Obama's recovery policies of big government have fallen far short of Reagan's recovery which focused on free market policies. If the Obama's recovery tracked the Reagan recovery there would be 6.6 million more jobs in America today.

267.title: Dr. Burgess, (R-TX) speaks during Joint Economic Committee Hearing on Gas Prices
267.description: Representative Dr. Burgess republican member of the JEC talks during the JEC hearing on " Gas Prices in the Northeast: Potential Impact on the American Consumer Due to Loss of Refining Capacity". He discusses current pending legislation to pull back mandated ethanol blends which are harmful to normal car engines, and there is a lack of studies and research to prove that these higher percentage of ethanol blends do not damage engines as supported tout.

268.title: Representative Duffy speaks during JEC hearing on Gas Prices
268.description: Congressman Duffy (R-WI) member of the Joint Economic Committee, speaks about the social costs of different fuel sources and the government's role of getting involved in markets to control and increase the prices of fuels to cover these social costs, including regulating fuels and fracking,  during the JEC hearing on April 26, 2012.

269.title: Congressman Duffy first round of questions during JEC hearing 4.26.12
269.description: Congressman Sean Duffy (R-WI) questions witnesses during the Joint Economic Commitee's hearing "Gas Prices in the Northeast: Potential Impact on the American Consumer Due to Loss of Refining Capacity". He speaks about future tax concerns for oil refiner companies and if those costs will be pushed onto consumers.

270.title: Mr. Brady's Second Round of Questions at JEC Hearing
270.description: Mr. Brady's second round of questions at JEC hearing on, "Gas Prices in the Northeast: Potential Impact on the American Consumer Due to Refining Capacity."

271.title: Senator Toomey Asks a First Round of Questions at JEC Hearing on April 26, 2012
271.description: Senator Toomey questions the witnesses at the JEC hearing on, "Gas prices in the Northeast: Potential Impact on the American Consumer Due to Refining Capacity."

272.title: Vice Chairman Brady's First Round of Questions at JEC Hearing on April 26, 2012
272.description: Vice Chairman Brady asks a first round of questions at JEC hearing on, "Gas Prices in the Northeast: Potential Impact on the American Consumer Due to Refining Capacity."

273.title: Mr. Brady's Opening Statement
273.description: Vice Chairman Brady's Opening Statement at the JEC hearing on, "Gas Prices in the Northeast: Potential Impact on the American Consumer Due to Refining Capacity."

274.title: Rep. Kevin Brady speaks on CNBC Friday April 20, 2012
274.description: Congressman Kevin Brady, Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee speaks on CNBC 4.20.12. Mr. Brady, speaks about  key elements to winning the presidential election in the fall. He also talks about the currently weak economic recovery, and how the Federal Reserve has taken too much action during the recovery. Mr. Brady introduced the Sound Dollar Act in March which would limit the Feds role in the future.

275.title: JEC Vice Chairman Brady during hearing on taxing capital
275.description: Rep. Brady (R-TX) asks the witnesses, during the Joint Economic Committee's hearing on "How Taxation of Capital Affects Growth and Employment", about if the Cobb Douglas model is widely accepted within economic literature on April 17, 2012. He also talks about what would happen with a major increase in the capital gains rate, in addition taxes on capital effect labor and real wages as well.

276.title: Mr.Brady's second round of questions at JEC taxing capital hearing
276.description: Rep. Kevin Brady (R-TX) vice chairman of the joint economic committee, discusses the need to reform the federal tax system and that the rate needs to change but the goal should be to have the most pro growth tax policy posible.

277.title: Rep. Brady final question and closing remarks during JEC hearing 4.17.12
277.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Rep. Brady, speaks about what happens when taxes on dividends goes up, how do businesses react, do they increase or decrease dividends when the tax rate changes.

278.title: Dr. Burgess presents an opening statment during JEC hearing on taxing capital
278.description: Dr. Burgess, (R-TX) discusses the complexity of the tax code and the hours and costs of compliance that is spent to file taxes in the United States. He believes that the tax code needs to be simplified and agrues for a flat tax rate.

279.title: Rep. Mulvaney (R-SC) questions witnesses at JEC hearing 4.17.12
279.description: Rep. Mulvaney (R-SC) speaks about the difference between the dynamic and static scoring and how it shows differences on the effects of changes in taxation on the economy. Is there a way to create a dynamic system that will provide a potential range of outcomes that would give us a better outlook of what the future would be under different changes in the tax code.

280.title: Senator Lee (R-UT) questions witnesses at JEC hearing 4.17.12 on taxing capital
280.description: Sen Lee speaks during JEC hearing "How Taxation of Capital Affects Growth and Employment" on tax day April 17, 2012. Sen Lee asks about how the compliance costs compare to the actual revenue received by the government. He also argues that all taxes and specifically corporate income taxes eventually fall on the consumers and workers.

281.title: Rep. Mulvaney speaks at JEC hearing on taxing capital 4.17.12
281.description: Rep. Mulvaney (R-SC) republican member of the Joint Economic Committee, talks to witnesses about how corporate tax rates encourage debt financing and how lowering the tax rate could discourage flows of debt and capital.

282.title: Senator Coats speaks during JEC hearing on taxing capital
282.description: Sen. Coats republican memeber of the Joint Economic Committee, questions witnesses about what might happen if the US lowers corporate tax rates, will other countries follow and lower their rates as well. Will decreasing corporate tax rates create a positive effect on the economy.

283.title: Senator Lee's second round of questions during JEC hearing 4.17.12
283.description: Senator Lee (R-UT) republican member of the Joint Economic Committee, asks witnesses about their personal ideal for reforming the American tax code in the future.

284.title: Rep. Kevin Brady presents his Opening Statement during JEC hearing on taxing capital
284.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Rep. Kevin Brady presents his opening statement tax day April 17, 2012, during JEC hearing "How the Taxation of Capital Affects Growth and Employment". Despite a growing body of empirical evidence on the adverse effects of taxing capital, President Obama and many Congressional Democrats are advocating a series of tax increases that will raise the cost of capital.

285.title: Rick Santelli talks about the Monthly Budget Statement for March 4.11.12
285.description: Rick Santelli discusses the most recent monthly budget statement for March which showed that US debt increasesd by $198 billion. He points out that if you tax all people that earn a million dollars or more a year, 1 million dollars it would only cover 1 month of deficit spending.

286.title: Santelli Exchange April 11, 2012
286.description: Rick Santelli discusses the upcoming 10 year debt offering from the US that will take place at 2 pm April 11, 2012. He provides an example that taxing the rich can not decrease the deficit. The US is spending way too much and is on a fiscally unsustainable path, deficit spending is over 100 billion each month.

287.title: JEC Vice Chairman Kevin Brady presents his closing remarks during JEC budget debate
287.description: Congressman Brady speaks about how Obama has failed on everything he had promised. After all the President's economic policies of massive federal spending, we still have fewer Americans working today than before the recession. He believes that now is the time to seriously look at the future of this country. We have two choices to stay the course or present a solution to the oncoming debt crisis.

288.title: Dr. Burgess speaks during the JEC budget floor debate
288.description: Rep. Dr. Burgess, (R-TX), member of the joint economic committee, discusses the need to repeal the new Health care system. He believes that the situation surrounding fixing the expanding health care costs is at the heart of the long term budget deficit situation.

289.title: Rep. Mulvaney speaks during the JEC Budget Floor debate
289.description: On March 28, 2012; Rep Mulvaney (R-SC) member of the Joint Economic Committee, debates the need for a balance budget and to decrease spending. Looking at other countries in similar situations countries that cut spending instead of increasing taxes have faired far better than countries that have raised taxes.

290.title: Rep. Sean Duffy (R-WI) speaks during the JEC Budget Floor Debate
290.description: Congressman Duffy Republican member of the Joint Economic Committee, discusses the need to cut spending to ensure fiscal stability in the future. He argues that tax policies are the reasons why jobs are being shipped overseas. Raising taxes will not balance the budget, even with a tax rate of 100% on the top two tax rates you still could not balance the budget.

291.title: Rep. Kevin Brady presents his opening statement during the JEC Budget debate
291.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady (R-TX) begins the JEC budget debate time during the House Budget proposal debate on March 28, 2012. Rep. Brady discusses economic reasons why he supports the budget proposed by Chairman Paul Ryan. He shows that it is private investment not government spending that spurs job growth. Also using comparisons between the Obama and Reagan recoveries from recessions, he shows that free market policies have proven to be much more successful than the big government policies imposed by the Obama administration.

292.title: Congressman Kevin Brady, speaks during JEC hearing on "Monetary Policy Moving Forward"
292.description: Rep. Brady talks about his new legislation on monetary policy moving forward. The Sound Dollar Act, introduced on March 8th, will restrict the Federal Reserve to a single mandate of price stability, but this does not totally ignore the goal to maximize employment. He asks witnesses to provide insight on issues that could come about on a move to restrict the Fed to a single mandate.

293.title: Rep. Kevin Brady during JEC Hearing on Monetary Policy, March 27, 2012
293.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady (R-TX) questions witnesses during the "Monetary Policy Moving Forward " hearing. Mr. Brady, believes by the Federal Reserve allocating credit to only specific segments in the market only politicizes the Fed and makes it more difficult for the Fed to unwind its policy when needed.

294.title: Sen. Lee Questions Witnesses at JEC Monetary Policy Hearing March 27th.
294.description: Senator Lee Republican memeber of the Joint Economic Committee, questsions witnesses during a hearing on "Monetary Policy Moving Forward", about why they think the US should require the Federal Reserve to move to a single mandate of price stability.

295.title: Sen. DeMint's Second Round of Questions, during JEC Monetary Policy Hearing
295.description: Senator DeMint (R-SC) speaks during the JEC hearing on "Monetary Policy Moving Forward", March 23, 2012. Sen DeMint starts the discussion on the difference between a free market based monetary policy versus a more centralized policy.

296.title: Sen. Lee Second Round of Questions at JEC Monetary Policy Hearing 3.27.12
296.description: Senator Lee (R-UT) talks during Joint Economic Committee, hearing "Monetary Policy Moving Forward", he asks witnesses how the credibility of the Federal Reserve has changed over time and how future interest rate increases could severely hurt the U.S. economy.

297.title: Senator Jim DeMint Questions Witnesses at JEC hearing March 27, 2012
297.description: Sen. Jim DeMint (R-SC) expresses his concern to witnesses of a lack of standards for monetary value, and there is no standard for monetary supply either. There is no institutional discipline, and yet the Federal Reserve is beginning to pay a key role in this country's fiscal situation.

298.title: Rep. Kevin Brady's Opening Statement at JEC hearing on Monetary Policy 3_27_12
298.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady (R-TX) presents his opening statement at the JEC hearing "Monetary Policy Moving Forward". The hearing is meant to question what role the Federal Reserve should play moving forward to ensure that the United States has the World's strongest economy in the world.

299.title: Rep. Kevin Brady (R-TX) on Fox Business March 23, 2012
299.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee Kevin Brady, discusses the upcoming court challenge against Obamacare. He also talks about the current situation surrounding the health care law and what steps need to be taken to improve the health care system.

300.title: Rep. Kevin Brady discusses his new Sound Dollar Act on Bloomberg 3.5.12
300.description: Joint Economic Committee Vice Chairman Kevin Brady (R-TX) talks to Bloomberg TV's Mark Compton about his new bill to reform the Federal Reserve. Mr. Brady seeks to return the Fed to the single mandate of price stability that the Fed operated under from the Reagan through Clinton years.

301.title: AEI event -A New Mission for the Fed: Remarks by Kevin Brady-
301.description: Rep. Kevin Brady (R-TX) speaks during AEI's event -A New Mission for the Fed- on March 5 2012. Rep. Brady, Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, discusses legislation that he will be introducing later this week -Sound Dollar Act- which will reform the Federal Reserve. He believes that the Fed should have a single mandate of price stability to ensure future growth and stability of the United States Economy.

302.title: Rep. Kevin Brady on CSPAN's Washington Journal February 14, 2012 (part 1 of 2)
302.description: Congressman Kevin Brady (R-TX), Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, and Ways and Means Committee Member, talks about the extension of payroll tax cut and unemployment benefits through the remainder of this year. He argues that there is a need for permanent tax restructuring and temporary tax breaks have little "bang for the buck". He also offers his opinion on the President's 2013 FY budget.

303.title: Rep. Kevin Brady on CSPAN's Washington Journal Feb. 14 2012 (part 2 of 2)
303.description: Congressman Kevin Brady (R-TX) speaks on various issues including the President's new budget proposal, social security solvency, future tax code reform, the need for entitlement reform, the MAP act, and other changes that need to be made in order to strengthen economic growth, during CSPAN's Washington Journal on February 14, 2012.

304.title: Rep. Mulvaney's second round of quesitons during JEC hearing on February 7, 2012.
304.description: Rep. Mulvaney, talks about how unemployment rate is dropping because the work force is shrinking. In the recent employment report the unemployment rate dropped to 8.3% but there are some troubling underlying facts that are going unnoticed .

305.title: Rep. Kevin Brady questions witnesses at JEC hearing on February 7, 2012
305.description: Rep. Keving Brady (R-TX),Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, expresses the need to extend payroll tax cuts and unemployment benefits for the rest of this year, but they have to be paid for. The payroll tax holiday of 2011 has already put a large hole in the Social Security trust fund. He also asks if there should be stricter requirements for unemployment benefits.

306.title: Rep. Mulvaney (R-SC) questions witnesses during JEC hearing on payroll tax and UI extension
306.description: Rep. Mulvaney, republican member of the Joint Economic Committee, asks what is wrong with drug testing as a requirement to receive unemployment insurance, during the JEC hearing: "Bolstering the Economy: Helping American Families by Reauthorizing the Payroll Tax Cut and UI Benefits".

307.title: Representative Duffy (R-WI), during JEC hearing on February 7, 2012.
307.description: Rep. Duffy, agrees that there is a need to help people who have fallen on hard times, but there needs to be a way to weed out the "bad apples" those who are abusing the system and soaking up the benefits when they shouldn't be.

308.title: Senator Lee speaks during Joint Economic Committee Hearing on the Payroll Tax and UI extensions
308.description: Senator Lee, askes witnesses during the JEC hearing on February 7, 2012, about how the extension of unemployment insurance benefits effects the length of time people are unemployed.

309.title: Rep. Kevin Brady's Opening Statement during JEC hearing on February 7, 2012.
309.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady, presents his opening statment at the JEC hearing: "Bolstering the Economy: Helping American Families by Reauthorizing the Payroll Tax Cut and UI Benefits". He agrees that these provisions need to be extended but they also need to be paid for in order to prevent future fiscal instability.

310.title: Rep. Mulvaney during the JEC's January Employment Report Hearing
310.description: Rep. Mulvaney asks about what week people typically come off of unemployment to come back into the workforce.

311.title: Rep. Mulvaney's second round of questions during JEC January's Employment Report Hearing
311.description: Rep. Mulvaney's asks what percentage of governmet jobs were lost compared to the government workforce in 2011, however we are still 5.6 million jobs short in the entire economy since the beginnig of the recession, which is about 4% of the entire labor force.

312.title: Rep. Mulvaney speaks during the Joint Economic Committee's January Employment Hearing
312.description: Rep. Mulvaney (R-SC), discusses the issues behind the decreasing labor force participation, as well as increasing numbers of part time workers for economic reasons, discouraged workers and marginally attached people. What levels of change in these categories should we expect to see in order to see unemployment come back down to a prerecession level.

313.title: Rep. Burgess' second round of questioning during JEC employment hearing
313.description: Rep. Burgess asks what happens when unemployment beneifts and insurance expire, what normally happens to the unemployment rate, during the Joint Economic Committee's Employment hearing for January's employment report.

314.title: Dr. Burgess first round of questions during JEC employment hearing in February
314.description: Dr. Burgess (R-TX) questions why the recovery has been so painfully slow, and much more prolonged compared to other recessions. He also brings to attention the correlation between the increasing minimum wage and unemployment rate, and if the number of growth in the job market continued to increase how long would it take to get back to prerecession levels.

315.title: Rep. Campbell (R-CA) speaks during JEC Employment Hearing 2.3.12
315.description: Mr. Campbell, asks about how the unemployment rate dropped down but the unemployment rate by widest measure did not change in January. The broadest number of unemployed / underemployed is currently at 15.1% far above the normally viewed unemployment rate which dropped to 8.3% in January.

316.title: Rep. Kevin Brady during Joint Economic Committee February Employment Hearing
316.description: Vice Chairman Kevin Brady (R-TX), questions Mr. Galvin of the BLS on the employment situation report for January, about if it is good news that payroll jobs have increase even though the labor force is decreasing. He also points out that hiring across the employment sector is not strong enough to suggest strong economic growth.

317.title: Dr. Burgess presents his opening statement during the JEC Employment Hearing on Feb. 3, 2012
317.description: Rep. Burgess (R-TX), argues that the private sector is what drives the United States economy. The government needs to get out of the way, reduce regulations and litigations on the private sector to allow further economic growth and expansion. Uncertainty in the future, is inhibiting private sector growth as well.

318.title: Rep. Brady provides his opening statement at the JEC hearing on the January Employment report
318.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady, presents his opening statment to the Committee and witnesses on the Bureau of Labor Statistics' January Employment Situation Report. Although the new payroll jobs have increased this encouraging data only masks the fact that labor force participation is the lowest it has been in almost 28 years, at 63.7%. In addition despite all of the stimulus and money spent by the President hiring levels have not increased higher than it was mid way through the recession.

319.title: Rep. Kevin Brady (R-TX) Speaks on Bloomberg Live Feb. 2, 2012
319.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady, talks on Bloomberg about his introduction of legistlation to limit the Federal Reserve to a single mandate, of price stability. He also discusses the problems involved in becoming more fiscally responsible without hurting the struggling economy.

320.title: Rep. Brady on Bloomberg Dec. 22, 2011 during the payroll tax cut extension showdown
320.description: Mr. Brady, is one of the conferee's selected by Speaker Boehner to negotiate the full year payroll tax cut extension. He speaks about what the committee has been able to do and what is their plan moving forward with only a few days remaining before payroll taxes increase.

321.title: Representative Kevin Brady talks on Fox Business Lou Dobbs Show Dec. 21, 2011
321.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, discusses the reason why the House GOP conferees are still in DC and are insisting a full year long payroll tax cut extension. He also provides his opinion and response to a recent Wall Street Journal article bashing the Republican House members for blocking the Senate bill.

322.title: Congressman Kevin Brady on Fox Business discussing the payroll tax extension situation
322.description: Rep. Brady, talks about how politically republicans are being blamed but are not at fault and are working in the best interests of Americans across the Country, during the payroll tax extension showdown.

323.title: Mr. Brady speaks on MSNBC about the payroll tax showdown in DC
323.description: Rep. Kevin Brady, one of the Republican House Members elected by Speaker Boehner to be on the conference committee talks about the situation in the Capitol on the payroll tax cut extension.

324.title: Mr. Brady talks on Fox News about the Payroll Tax Extension December 12, 2011
324.description: Rep. Kevin Brady (R-TX) talks about the strategy of the Conference Committee called by Speaker Boehner. Republicans will stay in DC until the job gets done to force a full year extension of the payroll tax cut.

325.title: Rep. Kevin Brady (R-TX) questions witnesses at JEC hearing on Nov. 17
325.description: Vice chairmand of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady, questions experts during JEC hearing on the effects of the implementation of a fair tax and who would be impacted the most by that type of change to the tax system.

326.title: Congressman Mulvaney at JEC hearing "Could Tax Reform Boost Business Investment and Job Creation?"
326.description: Rep. Mulvaney (R-SC) talks during a JEC hearing on taxes about the fact that half of the people that make money in this country don't pay federal income taxes and if everyone needs to pay taxes.

327.title: Mr. Duffy speaks at JEC hearing on November 17
327.description: Rep. Duffy talks about how capital goes to the best or most cost effective place. However raising taxes in America will make us less competitive on a global stage. There is a need to make the US more competitive internationally to encourage investment.

328.title: Rep. Campbell (R-CA) questions experts at Joint Economic Committee hearing on November 17, 2011
328.description: Rep. Campbell of the JEC asks what additional actions need to be taken to close the deficit gap, reduce spending, increase taxes, tax reform and or creation of a fair tax, during the hearing "Could Tax Reform Boost Business Investment and Job Creation?"

329.title: Mr. Duffy's Second Round of Questions at JEC Hearing 11.17.11
329.description: Rep. Duffy questions witnesses about their opinion on increasing taxes and future tax refrom, at the JEC hearing "Could Tax Reform Boost Business Investment and Job Creation?"

330.title: Sen. Coats at JEC hearing "Could Tax Reform Boost Business Investment and Job Creation?"
330.description: Republican Sen. Coats talks at the JEC hearing on November 17. He focuses on addressing the corporate tax rate and how it hinders competitiveness of the US internationally. He asks the experts' opinion on dropping the corporate tax rate as he suggests in legislation he is proposing.

331.title: Mr. Brady's First Round of Questions at JEC Hearing on Manufacturing November 16, 2011
331.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady, questions witnesses at the JEC hearing on Manufacturing and Infrastructure, about the failed results of the government funded stimulus in construction and manufacturing. Is there really a need for Obama's proposed infrastructure bank to help invest in infrastructure? Rather reducing regulations would create more bang for your buck results.

332.title: Vice Chairman's Brady's Second Round of Questions at JEC Manufacturing Infrastructure Hearing
332.description: Mr. Brady asks the panel if transportation authorities and officials would rather have Obama's proposed infrastructure bank or do they desire to fix their current trust funds. Other countries have moved toward private investment in infrastructure and the US should consider a similar change.

333.title: Rep. Mulvaney at JEC Hearing "Manufacturing in the USA: Paving the Road to Job Creation"
333.description: Rep. Mulvaney (R-SC) asks witnesses if we should see any different results from further government spending after major investments from the stimulus failed.

334.title: Rep. Mulvaney's Second Round of Questions at JEC hearing 11.16.11
334.description: Rep. Mulvaney dicussses the fact that states and federal government lack the funds to support infrastructure, and the issues surround the possible movement towards a more privatized infrastructure system.

335.title: Rep. Campbell questions witnesses at JEC hearing on Mfg. Infrastructure
335.description: Rep. Campbell (R-CA) talks to the witnesses about future infrastructure spending, and how to get private investment to fund public infrastructure projects.

336.title: Mr. Brady's Opening Statement at JEC Hearing November 16, 2011
336.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, presents his opening statement to the committee and witnesses at the JEC Hearing "Manufacturing in the USA: Paving the Road to Job Creation". He believes that congress should make it easier for the private sector to invest in transportation infrastructure which would reduce the stress on already cash strapped federal resources.

337.title: Rep. Brady's Second Round of Questions at the JEC Nov 4 Employment Hearing
337.description: Vice Chairman Kevin Brady ask Dr. Hall if a monthly job increase of 250,000 is enough to decrease the unemployment rate and to return the US to pre recession levels. Also he talks about the need to focus on private sector jobs rather than government jobs.

338.title: Dr. Burgess at JEC Employment Hearing 11-4-11
338.description: Dr. Burgess talks about how regulations and uncertainty have prevented the needed job growth necessary to reduce the unemployment rate.

339.title: Rep. Mulvaney 2nd Round of Questions at JEC Hearing Nov 4, 2011
339.description: Rep. Mulvaney is focusing on the inability of the Obama administration to create desired amount of 250,000 jobs a month needed to decrease the unemployment rate.

340.title: Rep. Mulvaney Questions Dr. Hall  at JEC Employment Hearing Nov 4, 2011
340.description: Rep. Mulvaney questions Dr. Hall during the Joint Economic Committee hearing -Employment Situation-, asking Dr. Hall about where the unemployment rate would be if the stimulus was not enacted in 2009.

341.title: Rep. Brady Questions Dr. Hall during JEC Employment Hearing
341.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, questions witness Dr. Hall, commissioner of the BLS, about how much monthly job growth is really needed to drop the unemployment rate. He also focuses on the number of workers in the workforce as it has hit 30 year lows.

342.title: Vice Chairman Brady's Opening Statement at JEC Employment Hearing
342.description: Joint Economic Committee Vice Chairman Kevin Brady present his opening statement to the committee and witness Dr. Hall, commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics during the JEC -Employment Situation- hearing on November 4, 2011

343.title: Mr.Brady interview with Andrea Mitchell 10_27_11
343.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady, voices his opinion on the special deficit reduction committee's progress and the recent proposal from democrats on the committee to reduce the deficit.

344.title: Vice Chairman Brady's Opening Statement at JEC Hearing 10.4.11
344.description: Rep. Kevin Brady, Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, presents his opening statement to the JEC and witness Ben Bernanke Chairman, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System during the JEC hearing "The Economic Outlook" on October 4, 2011.

345.title: Vice Chairman Brady's second round of questions during "Economic Situation" hearing
345.description: Vice Chairman of the Joint Economic Committee, Kevin Brady, asks Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke about the transparency of the Fed and the the value of the dollar and trade barriers and how they it effects the trade deficit with China.

346.title: Rep. Campbell's first round of questions at the JEC hearing "The Economic Situation"
346.description: Rep. Campbell raises issues about European's current situation and how actions in Europe can effect the US, specifically looking at the financial system. He also addresses the importance of the housing sector and what needs to be done to encourage growth in this sector.

347.title: Rep. Burgess questions Ben Bernanke during the JEC hearing on October 4, 2011
347.description: Dr. Burgess (R-TX) talks to Fed Chairman Bernanke on why corporations have over $1 trillion sitting on the sidelines of the US economy and why aren't corporations using their money, and what can be done to get corporations to invest these funds and encourage economic growth.

348.title: Rep. Duffy during the Joint economic Committee hearing on the economic situation
348.description: Congressman Duffy, asks Chairman Bernanke about the US secondary exposure through the European Banking system, and if the Chairman thinks that Europe will achieve success in the impending crisis. Rep. Duffy also focuses on the importance of shrinking the US debt now, since it will be more difficult to solve down the road.

349.title: Rep. Mulvaney (R-SC) at JEC hearing "The Economic Situation"
349.description: Mr. Mulvaney questions Chairman Bernanke depressed interest rates and increased borrowing by the Fed and how this effects inflation. Also asking if the Fed would be more successful working under a single mandate instead of the current dual mandate.

350.title: Senator  Dan Coats (R-IN) at "The Economic Situation" JEC Hearing
350.description: Senator Coats, speaks during the JEC hearing on Oct. 4, 2011, addressing the concern of the future fiscal stability of the US, and how can government eliminate the future uncertainty of the U.S. fiscal situation, therefore encouraging economic growth and confidence in the economy.

351.title: Sen. Lee's first round of questions at JEC Hearing October 4, 2011
351.description: Sen. Lee during the JEC hearing "The Economic Situation" questions witness Chairman Ben Bernanke, about the actions taken by the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates to record lows, and how will that effect individuals throughout the country, and where will interests go in the future.

352.title: Senator DeMint questions Chairman Benranke at JEC Hearing "The Economic Situation"
352.description: Sen. DeMint (R-SC) points out the unprecedented action of the Federal Reserve over the past few years. Questioning about how much did the Fed's balance sheet increased as a result of the Fed's dual mandate of price stability and to maximize employment.

353.title: Rep. Campbell's (R-CA) second round of questioning at JEC hearing
353.description: Rep. Campbell, asks Chairman Bernanke on October 4, 2011 during the JEC hearing "The Economic Situation", about the risk of the European crisis to the US through international financial connectivity, is there anything that government can do in the future to mitigate damage incase Europe does incur another financial crisis.

354.title: Dr. Burgess questions Ben Bernanke during Second Round of Questioning
354.description: Dr. Michael Burgess (R-TX), questions Chairman Bernanke during the Joint Economic Committee, hearing "The Economic Situation"  on October 4, 2011. Dr. Burgess, looks for the Chairman's insight on the future fiscal situation, and what plans were in place incase the government defaulted on the debt back in August.

355.title: Rep. Mulvaney's Second Round of Questions at JEC hearing October 4, 2011
355.description: Rep. Mulvaney (R-SC) discusses the policies taken by the Federal Reserve, and what are the possible future tools that the Fed are considering to implement if it finds the need to provided further stimulus to the economy.

356.title: Senator Lee (R-UT) second round of questions during JEC hearing "The Economic Situation"
356.description: Sen. Lee, questions Chairman Bernanke about the specifics of what needs to be done to reach fiscal responsibility, through spending cuts and or tax cuts. Some empirical evidence has shown  that steep fiscal cuts have assisted economies recover.

357.title: Rep. Brady Questions Chairman Ben Bernanke
357.description: JEC Vice Chairman Kevin Brady (R-TX) questions Chairman Ben Bernanke on how issues in Europe will effect the United States, and what tools the Fed would use to mitigate the effects of any financial crisis in Europe on the US.

358.title: Rep. Brady's Second Round of Questioning during September 21, 2011 Hearing

52.title: The Disastrous Impact of TrumpCare on the Opioid Crisis
52.description: Under the Republican health care plan, an estimated 24 million people will lose health coverage, including more than a million Americans who have been able to secure treatment for substance use disorders (SUDs) under the Affordable Care Act (ACA). At a time when the opioid and heroin epidemic is ravaging communities across America, costing billions of dollars a year, we cannot afford to take such a giant step backward in our efforts to combat the opioid and heroin epidemic. If Republicans succeed in repealing Medicaid expansion, Americans should expect pain from the opioid and heroin epidemic to get even worse: more people will go untreated because of lost insurance or rising costs, families and workplaces will continue to be pulled apart by the epidemic, hospitals and taxpayers will get stuck with the bill for uncompensated care, and the costs to our economy will continue to rise.
